name: Task 7: Modify App.vue to add device-based routing
description:
## Summary

The task involves adding mobile support to **codx-junior-ui**, a Vue.js desktop docking panel app using `dockview-vue` with 19 panels. The approach modifies only `App.vue` to conditionally render `<MobileLayout />` or `<Desktop />` based on a `useDevice()` composable that detects screen width. The mobile shell introduces `TopAppBar`, `BottomNavBar`, `MoreDrawer`, and `<keep-alive :max="3">` for memory-efficient panel rendering. Panels are tiered by priority (Primary/Secondary/Tertiary) with lazy loading and FIFO cache eviction replacing the desktop's `renderer: 'always'` strategy. `Desktop.vue` and all 19 panel components remain completely untouched.

                        # Conversation Summary: codx-junior-ui Mobile Layout Design

## Context
Design document (AS IS → TO BE) for adding mobile support to **codx-junior-ui**, a Vue.js desktop docking panel application.

---

## AS IS: Desktop Architecture

- **Root component:** `Desktop.vue` using `dockview-vue` library
- **19 registered dockable panels** (chat, tasks, files, wiki, kanban, knowledge, settings, etc.)
- **Panel lifecycle:** `$ui.showTab(name)` → `addAppPanel()` → `dockviewApi.addPanel()`
- **Persistence:** `dockviewApi.toJSON()` → `localStorage['dockview-layout']`
- **Rendering:** `renderer: 'always'` — all panels stay mounted in DOM simultaneously
- **Tab system:** Custom `Tab.vue` component per panel
- **Store integrations:** `$ui` (open apps, tab management) + `$chats` (chat rehydration on restore)
- **Auto-save triggers:** `onDidAddPanel`, `onDidRemovePanel`, `onDidLayoutChange`

### Key Limitations
- No mobile layout exists
- `renderer: 'always'` causes high memory usage with 19 panels
- `$ui` and `$chats` store contracts undocumented
- No deep linking / URL navigation
- No responsive breakpoints

---

## TO BE: Mobile Layout Design

### Core Principle
> Same stores + same panel components, different shell. `Desktop.vue` untouched.

### Device Routing (`App.vue`)
```
isMobile (window.innerWidth < 768) → <MobileLayout />
else → <Desktop />
```

### Shell Structure (`MobileLayout.vue`)
- **TopAppBar** — title + hamburger + notifications + avatar
- **Main area** — `<keep-alive :include="recentViews" :max="3">` wrapping active component
- **BottomNavBar** — 4 tabs: Tasks | Chat | Files | More
- **MoreDrawer** — bottom sheet grid with all 14 remaining panels

### Panel Priority Tiers
| Tier | Panels | Cache Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Primary | `tasks`, `chat`, `files` | Always cached, eagerly loaded |
| Secondary | `activity`, `projects`, `wiki`, `docs`, `profiles` | `defineAsyncComponent`, cached up to max=3 |
| Tertiary | `metrics`, `log-viewer`, `knowledge`, `knowledge_settings`, `settings`, `global-settings`, `account`, `file-finder`, `home` | Lazy loaded, not cached |

### Memory Strategy
- Replaces `renderer: 'always'` with `<keep-alive :max="3">`
- FIFO eviction of non-primary panels from cache
- `defineAsyncComponent` for secondary + tertiary panels

### State Persistence (`useMobileLayout.js`)
- Storage key: `mobile-layout`
- Saves: `{ activeView, recentViews }` to `localStorage`
- Restores on `onMounted`

### New Files
```
client/src/components/mobile/
  MobileLayout.vue
  BottomNavBar.vue
  TopAppBar.vue
  MoreDrawer.vue
client/src/composables/
  useDevice.js
  useMobileLayout.js
```
**Modified:** `App.vue` only  
**Untouched:** `Desktop.vue`, all 19 panel components

### Mobile UX Details
- Default view: `KanbanContainer` (tasks)
- `height: 100dvh` for dynamic viewport
- `env(safe-area-inset-*)` for notch/home bar support
- `-webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch` for iOS momentum scroll
- MoreDrawer renders as 3-column icon grid bottom sheet

### Deferred Items
- Deep linking (Vue Router integration needed)
- External wiki iframe/link strategy
- Auth/session management
- Full `$ui` / `$chats` store contracts for mobile chat hydration

---

## Keywords
`vue3`, `composition-api`, `dockview-vue`, `mobile-layout`, `responsive`, `keep-alive`, `defineAsyncComponent`, `bottom-navigation`, `bottom-sheet`, `safe-area-inset`, `100dvh`, `localStorage`, `panel-management`, `lazy-loading`, `memory-optimization`, `MobileLayout.vue`, `BottomNavBar.vue`, `TopAppBar.vue`, `MoreDrawer.vue`, `useDevice.js`, `useMobileLayout.js`, `$ui-store`, `$chats-store`, `desktop-first`, `codx-junior-ui`, `panel-tiers`, `FIFO-cache`, `dockview-layout`, `KanbanContainer`, `ChatView`, `dockview-theme-abyss`

# Task: Modify `App.vue` for Conditional Rendering Based on Device Type

## Overview

Modify the existing `client/src/App.vue` file to introduce device-aware conditional rendering. The application should dynamically serve either a **mobile layout** or the **existing desktop layout** based on the detected device type, without disrupting any current desktop functionality.

---

## Current State

The existing `App.vue` renders `Desktop.vue` which uses `dockview-vue` with 19 dockable panels, persistent layout via `localStorage`, and always-on rendering. This architecture must remain **completely untouched**.

---

## Required Changes

### 1. Imports to Add

```js
import { useDevice } from '@/composables/useDevice.js'
import MobileLayout from '@/components/mobile/MobileLayout.vue'
```

Keep the existing `Desktop` import exactly as-is.

### 2. Composition API Setup

Add a `<script setup>` section that:
- Calls `useDevice()` to get the `isMobile` reactive flag
- Exposes `isMobile` to the template

```vue
<script setup>
import { useDevice } from '@/composables/useDevice.js'
import MobileLayout from '@/components/mobile/MobileLayout.vue'

const { isMobile } = useDevice()
</script>
```

### 3. Template Changes

Replace the current single `<Desktop />` render with a conditional:

```html
<MobileLayout v-if="isMobile" />
<Desktop v-else />
```

- When `isMobile === true` → renders `<MobileLayout />`
- When `isMobile === false` → renders `<Desktop />` (identical to current behavior)

---

## Constraints

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| ✅ Preserve desktop | `Desktop.vue` and all 19 panel components must remain untouched |
| ✅ No logic changes | Only add imports and conditional rendering — no other App.vue logic changes |
| ✅ Composition API | Use `<script setup>` for `useDevice()` call only |
| ✅ TailwindCSS only | No scoped CSS |
| ✅ Component structure | Follow `setup → template → script` ordering |
| ❌ Do not refactor | Do not reorganize, optimize, or rewrite existing App.vue code |

---

## Expected File Structure

```vue client/src/App.vue
<script setup>
import { useDevice } from '@/composables/useDevice.js'
import MobileLayout from '@/components/mobile/MobileLayout.vue'

const { isMobile } = useDevice()
</script>

<template>
  <MobileLayout v-if="isMobile" />
  <Desktop v-else />
</template>

<script>
// existing App.vue script content preserved as-is
import Desktop from './components/desktop/Desktop.vue'

export default {
  components: {
    Desktop,
    // MobileLayout registered via script setup
  },
  // ... all existing options preserved
}
</script>
```

---

## Supporting Files (Already Planned — Do Not Create Here)

The following files are expected to already exist or be created separately:

- `client/src/composables/useDevice.js` — exports `useDevice()` returning `{ isMobile }`
- `client/src/components/mobile/MobileLayout.vue` — the full mobile shell

---

## Outcome

After this change:
- Desktop users (`window.innerWidth >= 768`) see **exactly** the same experience as before
- Mobile users (`window.innerWidth < 768`) are routed to `MobileLayout`
- No regressions in desktop panel persistence, store integration, or layout restoration
